basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 24.' and it opens 'Vers. 24. Quamobrem relinquet homo patrem et matrem. Hunc locum exponens Apostolus dicit:'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 24. Quamobrem relinquet homo patrem et matrem. Hunc locum exponens Apostolus dicit: Sacramentum hoc magnum est: ego autem dico in Christo et in Ecclesia (Eph. V, 32). Homo Christus intelligitur propter assumptam humanitatem. Qui dereliquit Patrem, quando de sinu paterno descendens | novus homo mundo visibilis apparuit, non deserendo Patrem, cum quo semper in divinitate inseparabiliter mansit. Dereliquit matrem, id est, Synagogam, de qua et carnem assumpsit. Adhaesit uxori suae, id est, conjunxit sibi Ecclesiam non habentem maculam aut rugam. Et factae sunt duo in carne una, id est, Christus qui caput, et membra ipsius, id est Ecclesia, sicut ipse Patrem orat pro primitiva sua Ecclesia, id est apostolis suis, dicens: Volo ut sint unum sicut et nos unum sumus (Joan. XVII, 21).
